title: Information-Theoretic Characterization of Macroscopic Chaos Emerging from the Chemical Master Equation
abstract: Open chemical reaction networks exhibit stochastic concentration dynamics at finite system sizes, whereas their macroscopic limit is governed by deterministic rate equations that can display chaos. In this Letter, we show theoretically that a rate of information loss constructed from two-time mutual information recovers the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy in the deterministic limit. We verify this result through numerical simulations of a Markov jump process for a three-species system involving seven reactions.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to quantify chaos in chemical reaction systems by analyzing information loss. It proves that the rate at which mutual information decays in the stochastic system converges to the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of the deterministic limit. This establishes a rigorous connection between information theory and the quantification of deterministic chaos in open, fluctuating physical systems.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates whether an information-theoretic measure derived from the stochastic Chemical Master Equation (CME) converges to the Kolmogorov-Sinai (KS) entropy in the macroscopic limit.
main_result: The rate of decrease of the two-time mutual information, $- rac{d}{dt}I(X(V)_t; X(V)_0)$, is shown to converge to the KS entropy ($h_{KS}$) in the large system-size limit ($V 	o \infty$).
method: The analysis involves relating the time evolution of mutual information to the conditional entropy, utilizing Gaussian approximations, and connecting the long-time growth rate to the sum of positive Lyapunov exponents.
model_or_system: The study uses open chemical reaction networks, specifically demonstrating the results with a modified CS14 three-species system. The dynamics are governed by the Chemical Master Equation (CME) in the stochastic regime and deterministic rate equations in the macroscopic limit.
key_observables: Mutual Information ($I$), Conditional Entropy ($H(\mathbf{X}(V)_t | \mathbf{X}(V)_0)$), Gaussian Entropy Increment ($\Delta H_G(V)$), and the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy ($h_{KS}$).
important_parameters: System size ($V$), time ($t$), and the Lyapunov exponents ($\lambda_i$) derived from the deterministic rate equations.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Gaussian approximation for the conditional distribution at large $V$ and assumes the convergence of the information loss rate to the KS entropy in the macroscopic limit.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows stochastic concentration time series approaching the deterministic limit. Figure 2 and Figure 4 illustrate the time evolution of the mutual information and the Gaussian entropy-growth rate, respectively, showing the convergence to $h_{KS}$ with finite-time corrections.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical link between information loss and KS entropy, derives the necessary mathematical tools using mutual information and conditional entropy, and then applies these tools to the CME in the large-system-size limit to confirm the convergence.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, information-theoretic bridge between the microscopic stochastic dynamics (CME) and the macroscopic deterministic chaos (KS entropy), which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems where noise and dissipation are key.
